name: claims
title: WWII unit location claims
description: One row per claim. Same header in every file under data/claims/. Vocabulary-backed fields refer to keys in schema/vocabularies.json. The claim's command relationships (who the unit was subordinate to, attached to or under the control of, with dates) are not stored in the claim file: they are rows of data/command_relations.csv, linked to the claim by data/command_relation_claims.csv (see schema/relations.schema.json); build/all_claims.csv carries the rebuilt `command_relationships` column. Values derived from other data are not stored in the claim files: location_name (place name + location_qualifier), location_temporal_offset_days, strength_status and the coordinate source note (see scripts/places.py); build/all_claims.csv carries them.
uniqueTogetherNote: A unit has at most one claim per date and event_type. Two claims may share the key only when they are in the same conflict group (conflict_group_id: sources that disagree) or when the pair is listed with a reason in data/claim_key_exceptions.csv (different actions of one kind on one day, one row per action).

repeatedColumns.description: Columns repeated from the unit table on every claim row so that a claim file is readable on its own. The validator requires them to equal data/units.csv.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.description: Unique id of the claim, C0001 onward. One row is one claim ("this unit was here on this date"). Never reused.

fields.name: conflict_group_id
fields.description: Shared by rows that make competing claims about the same unit and event (G001...). Blank if no known conflict.

fields.name: claim_status
fields.description: preferred, alternate or disputed (see vocabulary).

fields.name: unit_id
fields.description: Stable unit key, NATION-TYPE-NUMBER+ECHELONLETTER (for example US-INF-029D). Must exist in data/units.csv and match the file name.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date of the claim, YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: theater
fields.description: Primary theater of the claim (see vocabulary).

fields.name: nationality
fields.description: Nationality of the unit: the `name` of a row of data/nationalities.csv (foreign key; US, UK, Canada, Germany, ... Allied). Repeated from data/units.csv (must equal it). Matches the data/claims/<nationality>/ folder in lowercase.

fields.name: unit_name
fields.description: Unit name only, for example "29th Infantry Division".

fields.name: echelon
fields.description: Organisational level (see vocabulary).

fields.name: branch
fields.description: Service or arm (see vocabulary).

fields.name: parent_unit_id
fields.description: Unit id (from data/units.csv) of the operational parent on this row's date: the formation the unit was attached to or operating under, otherwise its standing parent. It must be one of the higher units of the relations the claim lists in data/command_relation_claims.csv (the relations themselves are rows of data/command_relations.csv; there is no command_relationships column in the claim file). Blank if the unit has no parent (top-level headquarters), or if no parent could be verified; then the claim lists one `unknown` placeholder relation (higher_unit_id blank, with a note). The organic parent, when different, is another relation of the claim.

fields.name: commander
fields.description: Commander on that date, rank and name as given by sources; "unknown" if not verified.

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: Decimal degrees WGS84.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: Decimal degrees WGS84.

fields.name: place_id
fields.description: The place the coordinate refers to: a row of data/places.csv (a named settlement or site, an area, sector or beach, or a front or axis). Replaces the free-text location_name, which is rebuilt in build/all_claims.csv from the place name and location_qualifier.

fields.name: location_qualifier
fields.description: Optional. What is specific to this claim about the place, as the sources word it: a context note ('division HQ Le Molay-Littry', 'point = Cheux') or the reserved first token `vicinity` (the claim says "vicinity of <place>"; further text follows after '; '). Blank when the claim is simply at the place. Never a place name that is not in places.csv.

fields.name: coord_override
fields.description: Optional. A reason, set only when this claim's latitude/longitude differ from the place's (another geocoder read of the same place, an approximate point). It names the coordinate source of the claim's own point and the distance to the place point ('OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Utah Beach, Manche, France); 290 m from the place point'). Blank when the claim uses the place's point: the validator requires the point to equal the place's exactly when this is blank and to differ when it is set.

fields.name: location_represents
fields.description: What the point stands for (see vocabulary).

fields.name: precision_km
fields.description: Judgment estimate of the radius in km within which the unit probably was (banded).

fields.name: operation_id
fields.description: Key of the most specific operation, battle, phase or campaign the claim belongs to, in data/operations.csv (for example OP-EPSOM, or the campaign row OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE when no named operation applies). Its parent chain gives the campaign, the umbrella (Overlord) and the named operation; build/all_claims.csv carries these as derived columns. The claim's date should lie inside the operation's dates; a claim just outside needs a row in data/operation_exceptions.csv.

fields.name: composing_units
fields.description: Subordinate units that are a unit of data/units.csv: `;` list of unit_ids (foreign key to units.unit_id), listed when first given or when they change. Blank (with composing_text blank too) means unchanged from the unit's previous row; "unknown" means no data. Components that are not a unit of the table (regiments, battalions, companies, groups) go in composing_text. build/all_claims.csv derives `composing_units_names`.

fields.name: composing_text
fields.description: Free text for the composition that is not a unit of data/units.csv, as a `;` list (a `;` inside parentheses does not split): regiments, battalions, companies, remarks. An entry `<unit_id> (<qualifier>)` is the qualifier of a unit listed in composing_units (for example `GER-PZ-002D (elements)`). No relationship prefix such as `attached:` (how a unit is attached belongs in data/command_relations.csv); an entry never repeats the name of a unit that has an id. A row whose composing_units and composing_text are both blank is unchanged from the unit's previous row; composing_text alone is a composition made only of non-unit components; "unknown" in composing_units means no data and composing_text is then blank.

fields.name: established
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was formed.

fields.name: disestablished
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was disbanded.

fields.name: destroyed
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was destroyed.

fields.name: confidence
fields.description: Numeric 0-1 confidence by rubric (see vocabulary).

fields.name: source
fields.description: The readable citation: URLs separated by " | ". Every row needs at least one URL, and each URL must resolve to an id in `reference_ids`. The coordinate source is not part of it: it is the place's `coord_reference_id` and `coord_source_note` (data/places.csv), or `coord_override` for a claim with its own point.

fields.name: reference_ids
fields.description: Stored links to the references that support this claim: reference_ids from data/references_meta.csv (R###), separated by ";", in citation order. The source of truth for claim-to-reference links (build/claim_references.csv and the claims_count of data/references.csv are built from it). The URLs in `source` stay as the readable citation and must resolve to ids listed here. Every claim needs at least one; a claim at confidence 0.9 should have references from at least two different source families (warning). The role of a link (event, date, location, command_relationship, strength) is in data/claim_reference_roles.csv; a link with no row there is "general".

fields.name: source_locator
fields.description: Where in a reference the claim is supported, as "R398: p. 285, 289; R407: p. 36" (reference_id, then page, chapter or section), separated by ";". Only ids that are in reference_ids. Blank where the citation gives no page; nothing is guessed. Filled from URL fragments (#page285) of the original citation.

fields.name: event_type
fields.description: One primary event type (see vocabulary).

fields.name: current_activity
fields.description: Short phrase (about 120 characters at most) saying the one action the sources document for the unit on that date at that place; lower-case, free text. No inferred direction or result; extra detail goes in notes.

fields.name: engaged_with
fields.description: Enemy units fought on that date: `;` list of unit_ids (foreign key to units.unit_id). Blank = no combat that day; "unknown" = combat with no opponent identified (the only sentinel). An opponent that is a named unit but not yet in the table gets a placeholder unit; a generic opponent goes in engaged_note. build/all_claims.csv derives `engaged_with_names`.

fields.name: engaged_note
fields.description: Free text for opponents that cannot be a unit id: an air force, naval forces, an unnamed formation ('British forces (Gold Beach sector; unit not named by CMH)'). `;` list; a `;` inside parentheses does not split. Never repeats the name of a unit that has an id; no `attached:` prefix. Blank when engaged_with says it all.

fields.name: strength_json
fields.description: Optional JSON object with sourced strength figures: {"basis","as_of","personnel","vehicles","vehicle_count_type","scope","status","source","note"}; scope (whole_unit, sub_force, sector) says what the figure covers and is required whenever personnel is present. `status` (full, reduced or heavily_depleted; vocabulary strength_json_status) is the qualitative strength a source states; a record with a status needs no personnel or vehicles figure. build/all_claims.csv derives `strength_status` from it (destroyed when the destroyed flag is true, unknown when there is no status). See docs/methodology.md. Blank where no source gives figures or a status.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free text: what the source says, caveats, source conflicts, change history.

fields.name: location_date
fields.description: Optional. The date the coordinate is actually documented for, when it differs from date (for example the date of the command post list the point was taken from). Blank when the coordinate is for the claim's own date or the date is not known.

fields.name: location_basis
fields.description: Optional. How the coordinate relates in time and place to date (see vocabulary location_basis). Blank on rows not yet reviewed.
